observations: The page number «40» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01: «Kalender» continues «dass im julianischen» at the end of p. 39 (JP2 0071, L36).

L08-L28. Checked: 1363 is 48 × 28 + 19; the Seleucid year 1363 began on 1 October 1051, so that its March is March 1052, a leap year of the Julian calendar, and 1 March 1052 was a Sunday, 5 March a Thursday. 1437 is 51 × 28 + 9; 1 January 1126 was a Friday and 26 January a Tuesday, the weekday of the text (p. 37, JP2 0069). 2224 is 79 × 28 + 12; 1 October 1912 of the Julian calendar was a Monday and 10 October, 23 October of the Gregorian calendar, a Wednesday. The Julian calendar repeats its weekdays after 28 years, four leap cycles of 1461 days, 5844 days or 834 weeks.

L38-L40: the correspondence of the tables, set in columns: the ditto marks „ stand under «Batt.», «Kh.» and «Tafel»; the list goes on on p. 41. Each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|». L32-L36: «Batt.», «Nallino», «Maslama al-Madjrīṭī», «Kh.» and «Maslamas» spaced.

As printed: «addiren» and «giebt» (L17), «addieren» and «gibt» (L25); «die Note 2» (L27), where L12 and L19 have «Nota»; «adar» (L09) upright, as the spelling of the tables, after the italic «ādhār» (L08); «julianischen» italic in L16 and L23, upright in L15. L12: «„Mart.“», the abbreviation in italics within upright quotation marks.
The colons and the question marks stand after the thin space of the edition (9-13 px measured).
